subject: StrataHub marketplace: SDK exemption & rollout coordination
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@stratahub.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Partner Ops <partners@stratahub.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: StrataHub marketplace listing + SDK exemption request

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for taking this call last week. StrataHub is ready to proceed with a Redwood marketplace listing, but we have a couple of asks that came up from our engineering and legal teams: 

- Our integration bundles a proprietary connector SDK (closed-source) that we cannot publish. We are asking whether Redwood can accept an SDK-exemption model (we’d host the connector in our environment and surface it via the marketplace listing).
- We’ve attached a short summary of the SDK boundaries and integration_requirements.xlsx so your infra team can confirm compatibility.

Can you confirm what product and security gates we’d need to clear for an exception? Also can we get an expected timeline for listing (targeting early July)?

Attachments: stratahub_sdk_summary.pdf, integration_requirements.xlsx

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform Partnerships
StrataHub

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@stratahub.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StrataHub marketplace listing + SDK exemption request

Alex —

Appreciate the clear summary and the files. Looping in Karthik (product) and Marissa (partner ops) — a few initial notes from my side: 

1) High-level feasibility: We can consider an SDK-exemption pattern (listing that points to a partner-hosted connector) but it will require a narrow set of controls before we can publish: an agreed security checklist, runtime compatibility validation, and a documented failure/fallback behavior so our SLA routing can handle outages.

2) What we need from StrataHub: a short architecture diagram that shows where the SDK runs, a support contact for incident escalation, and confirmation that no customer data is stored in your SDK layer (or details if it is). Please include that in the next version of stratahub_sdk_summary.pdf.

3) Timeline: If we get the updated artifacts by EOD Wednesday (May 26), product + infra can triage and give a go/no-go for a limited pilot by June 15. Full listing (marketplace page + GTM) would be on a July window, pending legal & security review.

Karthik / Marissa — can you weigh in on technical blockers and whether we need Dev to run a short compatibility test? Dev team may need a light test harness.

Thanks —
Irene
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Alex Kim <alex.kim@stratahub.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StrataHub marketplace listing + SDK exemption request

Thanks for the context. From a product/engineering lens a few concrete asks: 

- Compatibility checklist: We need a matrix mapping StrataHub SDK endpoints to the Redwood runtime integration points (auth, KV cache usage, streaming token semantics). If the SDK modifies tokenization or does custom caching, that is a blocking item.

- Test surface: Dev, can you provide a small hosted test harness (Docker image) we can run in our QA cluster to validate request/response shapes and latency profiles? If StrataHub cannot publish the image, a private upload to our S3 for temporary test is fine.

- Failure modes: We require a documented graceful-degradation plan. If partner is unavailable, Redwood must be able to route to a fallback connector or model variant without customer-visible errors.

If StrataHub can provide the compatibility matrix + a temporary test payload by May 26, we can run a light validation (3–4 days) and report back.

-JK (Karthik)
Principal Product Manager, Serving

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@stratahub.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StrataHub marketplace listing + SDK exemption request

Alex / team —

Quick commercial and ops notes from Partner Ops: 

- We can support a partner-hosted connector in the marketplace but we will surface a clear badge/notice on the listing that the partner hosts the connector and that it runs under partner SLA. That badge language will be included on the draft listing for review.

- Legal will want a short MOU that covers support SLAs and incident escalation. I’ve attached a first-pass contract_redlines_v1.pdf; please provide counterpoints.

- GTM: to hit a July public listing we need the technical sign-off by June 16 and legal sign-off by June 23. That aligns with the June 15 pilot window Karthik suggested.

Jonas — can you confirm we have capacity on the listing calendar and content support?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@stratahub.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@stratahub.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StrataHub marketplace listing + SDK exemption request

Marissa / Irene —

Thanks — we’ve reviewed the contract redlines and attached our responses (contract_redlines_v1.pdf). We will update stratahub_sdk_summary.pdf to include the architecture diagram and the explicit data flow statements you requested and upload to the HubSpot deal record (link below) by EOD Wednesday.

We’re also prepared to provide a private Docker image for the test harness; I’ll coordinate a secure upload with Dev Patel.

Link: https://hubspot.com/deal/SH-2389

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform Partnerships, StrataHub
